title: Comment on arXiv:2604.27678
summary: Shuang-Jie Liu et al. (arXiv:2604.27678) reported that the momentum-dependent nuclear mean field (MDI) with $K_0 = 230$ MeV 'can fit fairly' the experimental data for Au + Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 3$ GeV, whereas the momentum-independent nuclear mean fields (MID) with $K_0 = 230$ MeV and $K_0 = 380$ MeV 'can only partially describe' the experimental results. We quantify these statements by performing $χ^2$ goodness-of-fit tests for the comparison between the theoretical calculations and the experimental distributions presented in that work. For the complete set of data, all three calculations show highly statistically significant disagreement with the experimental data, with (p-value) p < 0.001. For the $0-10\%$ centrality class, however, the MDI calculation with $K_0 = 230$ MeV gives p = 0.49, indicating no statistically significant disagreement with the experimental data for the proton transverse-momentum distributions and the rapidity dependence of the mean transverse momentum, whereas both MID calculations give p < 0.001. For the $10-40\%$ centrality class, the analysis of the directed flows of protons, $K^+$ mesons, and $Λ$-hyperons gives the largest p-values for MDI with $K_0 = 230$ MeV and MID with $K_0 = 380$ MeV, with p = 1.00 and p = 0.97, respectively. In contrast, the analysis of the corresponding elliptic flow data gives p < 0.001 for all three calculations. Our results demonstrate that the qualitative statements 'fit fairly' and 'only partially describe' depend substantially on the particular observables and centrality classes considered and cannot by themselves establish statistically acceptable agreement between the calculations and the experimental data.

title: Competitive constraints on exotic tensor currents from $EC/β^+$ ratios
summary: We introduce the ratio of electron capture to positron decay rates of unstable nuclei as a probe for exotic tensor currents in the electroweak sector. We calculate nuclear structure corrections and newly derived radiative corrections and obtain competitive limits on exotic tensor couplings using historically available data to find $\varepsilon_T = (1.06 \pm 0.76)\times 10^{-3}$ which is competitive with collider searches and the global $β$-decay database. In doing so, we resolve a 50-year-old tension in the strongly hindered $^{22}$Na transition by retaining higher-order operators, obtaining a consistent description of its different weak-decay observables. Finally, we discuss the potential of this method to significantly improve tensor constraints using modern cryogenic quantum sensors.

title: Separating entanglement at emission from femtoscopic correlations
summary: We investigate how femtoscopic correlations modify the relation between the spin entanglement of emitted particle pairs and that of pairs selected at a given relative momentum. For two spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ particles, we show that the momentum-selected spin state can be entangled even when the corresponding state at emission is separable. We derive a momentum-dependent separability criterion that determines whether the observed spin correlations require entanglement at emission. As an application, we consider a pair of identical $Λ$ hyperons, for which quantum statistics and final-state interactions affect the singlet and triplet spin channels differently at low relative momentum. Our results provide a framework for using experimentally accessible spin correlations to investigate entanglement at emission.

title: Deconfinement and the Charge Susceptibility Matrix of QCD
summary: At sufficiently high temperatures, lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) calculations predict that nuclear matter undergoes a rapid crossover to a novel, deconfined state known as the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), in which quark flavors essentially behave like independent particles. Here we explore the nature of this transition by introducing two new thermodynamic observables which we refer to as the diagonality and the rescaled curvature of the QCD equation of state (EoS). By comparing these observables in the case of lattice QCD calculations with those of simple toy models and more sophisticated hadronic resonance models, we show that both the diagonality and the rescaled curvature provide complementary insights into the degree of independence between different quark flavors and the underlying degrees of freedom in the system as functions of temperature. We propose that these observables may help to clarify the nature of the transition region and the onset of deconfinement in nuclear matter.

title: Letter of Intent for Alpha Knockout from Nuclei in Hard Exclusive Processes with ALERT
summary: We propose to measure hard exclusive $α$-knockout reactions from the light $α$-conjugate nuclei $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$Ne using electron scattering. Three reaction channels will be measured for the first time on the same target set: (i) the quasi-elastic knockout $(e, e' α)$ knockout, which establishes a baseline against $α$-clustering model calculations and tests final-state-interaction (FSI) models; (ii) coherent deeply virtual Compton scattering (DVCS) on a bound $α$, which provides a quark-level probe of the bound system through the beam-spin asymmetry; and (iii) coherent vector-meson production ($φ$ and J/{$ψ$}) on a bound $α$, which probes the gluon distribution of the bound cluster through two-gluon exchange. The central observables are ratios of cross sections and beam-spin asymmetries between the bound $α$ in $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$ Ne and the free $^4$He ground state. Together these measurements directly address the question of the role of QCD in the structure of light nuclei : do the quark and gluon distributions of an $α$ embedded in a heavier nucleus differ from those of a free 4He, and do those modifications track the increasing $α$-clustering strength along the $α$-conjugate chain? The measurement will use the 12 GeV CEBAF accelerator in Hall B with the CLAS12 spectrometer instrumented with the ALERT low-energy recoil detector and high-pressure gas straw targets. ALERT, which replaced the CLAS12 silicon vertex tracker, was successfully commissioned and operated during Run Group L (RG-L) from April through August 2025. It uniquely provides identification of low-momentum recoiling light ions (p, d, t, $^3$He, and $^4$He) close to the beamline at the high luminosities required by these exclusive channels.

title: Higher-order corrections to beta decays and nuclear structure
comment: Chapter submitted to Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics. Comments are welcome
summary: Precision measurements of nuclear $β$ decay offer a powerful route to tests of physics beyond the Standard Model, but interpreting measurements spectra and correlation observables requires control of subtle nuclear-structure effects. This chapter develops a framework for calculating higher-order corrections--small contributions that can become important at the precision sought in searches for new interactions. After motivating their role in $β$-decay observables (with radiative corrections treated in the accompanying chapter), we introduce the relevant kinematics and multipole expansion of the shape factor, identify the subleading contributions, and present the impulse-approximation multipole operators. We then describe the nuclear many-body methods used to obtain the required states and transition densities, and derive the corresponding operator matrix elements in the harmonic-oscillator basis. Taken together, these ingredients enable systematic calculations of nuclear shape factors beyond the long-wavelength approximation, including higher-order multipoles where needed. By helping distinguish Standard-Model recoil effects from possible signatures of new physics, this framework supports the interpretation of increasingly precise $β$-decay experiments.

title: The 3He(α,γ)7Be γ-ray angular distribution: measured, and calculated by effective field theory
comment: Submitted to Phys. Rev. C as a Letter
summary: The 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be reaction takes place in several distinct astrophysical scenarios. First, in solar hydrogen burning, 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be controls the competition between the pp-I chain, on the one hand, and the pp-II and -III chains, on the other hand. Its rate directly affects the solar model predictions for the well-measured 7Be and 8B solar neutrino fluxes, which can in principle be used as solar thermometer. Second, in Big Bang nucleosynthesis, 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be is the main production channel for primordial 7Li, the decay product of 7Be. Finally, the reaction is believed to produce radioactive 7Be in astrophysical novae. The cross section of this reaction has been studied previously using different methods, namely 7Be activation, 7Be recoil detection, and in-beam γ-ray detection. The latter studies have in many cases been performed with just one detector in close geometry. Here, for the first time a comprehensive measurement of the 3He(α,γ)7Be γ-ray angular distribution is reported. Altogether 22 high-purity germanium detectors were used, arranged at 27-145 degrees angle with respect to the beam direction. Data were taken at 442-1213 keV center-of-mass energy. In addition, one data point for the astrophysical S-factor was obtained with the activation method. The angular data are compared with the predictions from a hybrid theoretical approach, where the E1 transitions are modeled using a cluster-based effective field theory (EFT) while the M1 and E2 transitions within an EFT-inspired framework. Good agreement is found, if the interference among these multipolarities is taken into account in the theory.

title: The $ΣN$ threshold structure in the $K^-d\toπ^-Λp$ reaction
summary: The $Λp$ invariant-mass spectrum near the two physical $ΣN$ thresholds in the $K^-d\toπ^-Λp$ reaction is studied as a probe of the low-energy $ΣN$ interaction. The reaction is formulated up to two-step processes, and the coupled $Λp$, $Σ^+n$, and $Σ^0p$ channels are described within a constant-$K$-matrix model constrained by spin-triplet scattering lengths. The dependence of the $ΣN\toΛp$ conversion amplitude on these scattering lengths is examined, and the relation between its line shape and nearby pole positions is investigated. The resulting invariant-mass spectra are studied at different incident kaon momenta and compared qualitatively with existing experimental data. The effects of the spin-singlet $YN$ amplitude and the deuteron wave function are also examined. The line shape near the $ΣN$ thresholds is found to be particularly sensitive to the complex spin-triplet $I=1/2$ $ΣN$ scattering length, indicating that measurements of this spectrum can provide useful constraints on the low-energy $ΣN$ interaction.

title: Asteroseismology of Neutron Stars with Axion-Like Particle Mediated Dark Matter
summary: We examine the impacts of dark matter (DM) on the observables of the neutron star (NS). The interaction of DM with nucleons intermediate by axion-like particles (ALPs), and the DM-admixed NS (DNS) is formulated in the framework of the relativistic mean field (RMF) formalism. The effects of the DM on the NS are characterized by two parameters: DM Fermi momentum ($q_f$) and DM mass ($m_χ$). By varying these two parameters, we investigate how the NS's mass, radius, and tidal deformability are altered. Furthermore, we study how the ALP-mediated DM impacts the stability of the NS through the analysis of radial oscillations. In addition, the nonradial oscillation has been investigated by calculating its fundamental mode frequency in the DNS and analyzed how the ALP-mediated DM modifies its behavior.

title: Representation dependence of the neutron-proton kinetic energy in adiabatic deuteron stripping
summary: The adiabatic distorted-wave approximation (ADWA), the standard model for deuteron stripping and pickup, depends on the neutron-proton interaction through the form factor $V_{np}φ_d$. With nonlocal nucleon potentials, the neutron-proton kinetic energy averaged with this form factor shifts the energy at which the nucleon-target potentials are evaluated, and ADWA cross sections become sensitive to the choice of interaction. I ask whether this sensitivity reflects short-range neutron-proton structure. A unitary transformation of the neutron-proton Hamiltonian with the AV18 interaction, confined to short distances, represents the same interaction differently and preserves the two-body scattering matrix, the deuteron binding energy, and both asymptotic normalizations. It raises the weighted kinetic energy from 218 to 313 MeV, a change equal to more than half the range spanned by the five realistic interactions studied, while the finite-range coefficient, which controls low-momentum transfer, hardly moves. The weighted kinetic energy is dominated by the variance of the kinetic energy, which the high-momentum components control, whereas the finite-range coefficient is set by the spatial extent of the form factor. A dependence on $V_{np}$ carried by the weighted kinetic energy can therefore arise from the representation of the interaction alone, and does not by itself measure its short-range content.

title: Universal relations for hybrid stars and their quark cores: a systematic scan of the quark-matter parameter space
summary: Universal, equation-of-state (EOS) insensitive relations among the global properties of compact stars are well established for hadronic neutron stars and for self-bound strange stars. We ask whether analogous relations hold for the quark core of a hybrid star, and whether the core can be constrained from the surface. Describing quark matter with the three-flavor MIT bag model with repulsive vector interactions, matched to the hadronic DD2 EOS through a Maxwell construction, we scan the full $(B^{1/4},G_V)$ plane and obtain 1112 hybrid EOSs with maximum masses above $2\,M_\odot$, broadly compatible with current multimessenger constraints. For every stable configuration we evaluate the mass, radius, moment of inertia, and tidal deformability both at the stellar surface and at the boundary of the quark core. Global quantities follow the relations of hadronic stars---the $I$--Love relation to within $0.5\%$---while core quantities follow those of self-bound strange stars with median deviations of $6$--$9\%$. We explain the latter by expanding the structure of the core in powers of its compactness: to first order, the core mass, baryon mass, moment of inertia, and tidal deformability depend only on the compactness and on the properties of the hadron--quark interface, chiefly the ratio $ξ=p_{\rm tr}/\varepsilon_+$ of transition pressure to quark energy density. The strange-star relations are the $ξ\to0$ member of this family, and the deviations from them measure $ξ$. The fractional core mass and radius of all configurations follow the normalized mass profile of the star, and no global observable allows the core size to be inferred. Evanescent cores dominate the viable parameter space, while sizable cores require low bag constants and strong vector couplings.

title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
summary: The question of the link between the nucleon properties and the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, both being composed of quarks and gluons, is investigated by adopting a soliton model to describe internal nucleon properties and a direct mapping between nucleon and quark matter to obtain the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. We compare $π+ω$ and $π+ω+ρ$ soliton models and analyze the presence of a pressure singularity at the nucleon center due to the $ρ$ field. This singularity impacts the equation of state in ultra-dense matter. Only the pressure derived from the canonical energy-momentum tensor has a singularity, while the Belinfante pseudo-gauge transformation of the energy-momentum tensor generates an internal pressure without a singularity. We then investigate predictions for the equation of state of ultra-dense matter based on different prescriptions for the nucleon pressure. It is shown that none of the prescriptions agree with the thermodynamical pressure defined in uniform matter. The mismatch between any equation of state and the thermodynamical one questions the simplicity of the direct mapping between finite-size nucleon properties and uniform matter as well as the role of the nucleon surface in the internal energy density and the pressure.

title: Contribution of incomplete fusion to the evaporation residue cross sections in the $^{30}$Si$+^{186}$W reaction
summary: The formation of the evaporation residues in the $^{30}$Si$+^{186}$W reaction leading to the compound nucleus $^{216}$Ra$^*$ has been studied in the framework of the dinuclear system (DNS) model. The capture, complete fusion, quasifission, and incomplete fusion cross sections have been calculated at the collision energies $E_{c.m.}=107.6-172.2$MeV by averaging over the orientation angles of the axial symmetry axes of the deformed $^{30}$Si and $^{186}$W nuclei. The incomplete fusion is considered as the breakup of the DNS with the emission of the $α$ particle from its very mass-asymmetric configuration, which is populated by the nucleon transfer in collisions with large orbital angular momentum. The survival probabilities of the excited $^{216}$Ra and of the conjugate nucleus $^{212}$Rn formed after the $α$-particle emission have been calculated using the statistical model. It is shown that the complete fusion is the main source of the evaporation residues at the lower collision energies, while above $E_{c.m.}=128$MeV the Rn isotopes formed in the incomplete fusion give more than half of the calculated evaporation residue cross section. The sum of both contributions describes the slow decrease of the measured total evaporation residue cross section at these energies, where the yield of the Ra isotopes decreases by an order of magnitude. The calculation of the de-excitation of $^{216}$Ra$^*$ with the emission of protons and $α$ particles shows that the contribution of the complete fusion to the cross sections of the isotopes $^{212}$Rn and $^{211}$Rn is negligible, and these isotopes are formed in the incomplete fusion. The fusion probability calculated for the partial waves $\ell\leq30\hbar$ is about 0.75 in comparison with the value $0.57\pm0.08$ extracted from the experimental data at the same collision energies.

title: Finite-Temperature Equations of State for Neutron-Star Mergers within the Quark Mean-Field Model
summary: We extend the quark mean-field (QMF) model to finite temperature and systematically investigate the thermodynamic properties of uniform nuclear matter, using the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model as a reference. For each model, we consider two parameter sets calibrated to the same selected nuclear-matter saturation properties but with different nucleon Dirac effective-mass ratios at saturation. We examine the effective nucleon mass and the composition of $β$-equilibrium matter, together with the free energy, energy density, pressure, entropy, and heat capacities of symmetric nuclear matter, pure neutron matter, and $β$-equilibrium matter. The QMF and RMF models exhibit similar qualitative trends, but their predictions increasingly differ at high density, where the effective masses have distinct density dependences. These differences are particularly evident in the thermal pressure and thermal index. For the two parameter sets considered in this work, we further provide compact analytical representations of the thermal index, $Γ_{\rm th}(ρ_{\rm b},T,β)$ over baryon densities of 0.08-1.0 $\rm fm^{-3}$, temperatures of 5-100 MeV, and isospin asymmetries of 0-1. The fits reproduce the numerical results with an accuracy better than $2\%$ and can be directly implemented in binary neutron-star merger simulations. This study establishes a finite-temperature extension of the QMF framework and provides a basis for future assessments of how a quark-structure-based description of nuclear matter affects thermal support and post-merger dynamics in binary neutron-star mergers.

title: Exact solution of adiabatic time dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov inertia for fission
summary: An efficient method to exactly compute the adiabatic time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov collective vibrational inertias typical of fission is proposed. The method uses the quasiparticle finite amplitude method to invert the stability matrix of linear response. A comparison with other approaches, such as the exact generator coordinate method inertia and the associated cranking non-perturbative approximation, is conducted. It is found that the behaviour as a function of the collective variable (mass quadrupole moment) is essentially the same in the four cases considered, and substantially differs from the commonly used perturbative approach. It is also found that the magnitudes of the inertias are to a good extent related by single factors that seem to be connected with the effective mass of the energy density functional used.

title: Femtoscopic parameters of pion emission sources in EPOS4 Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV
summary: Three-dimensional femtoscopy probes the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision-energy dependence of Lévy source parameters may reveal the evolution of strongly interacting matter and possible signatures of the QCD phase diagram. We previously studied the excitation function of three-dimensional Lévy source parameters for pion pairs in Au+Au collisions with EPOS4, analyzing the pair-distance distribution \(D(ρ)\) through one-dimensional projections. Here, we analyze the full three-dimensional source distribution and correlation function directly. We construct \(D(ρ_{\rm out},ρ_{\rm side},ρ_{\rm long})\) as a 3D histogram, transform it into \(C(q_{\rm out},q_{\rm side},q_{\rm long})\) using a Fast Fourier Transform, and fit the correlation function with the analytic Lévy formula. This approach can reduce biases arising when one-dimensional projections are used to describe a non-elliptical source. We apply the method across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan range and compare the extracted energy dependence with results from the projection-based method and recent UrQMD calculations. We focus on the out-side observables \(R_{\rm diff}^{2}=R_{\rm out}^{2}-R_{\rm side}^{2}\) and \(R_{\rm out}/R_{\rm side}\), whose different energy dependences in EPOS4 and UrQMD may illuminate the roles of emission duration and source dynamics. This work establishes a direct three-dimensional framework for comparison with future femtoscopic measurements and for exploring possible non-monotonic structures associated with the QCD phase diagram.

title: Shear viscosity from fluctuations in linearized relativistic hydrodynamics
summary: In this work we incorporate thermal fluctuations into fluid-dynamic simulations with the vHLLE code, in linear approximation. The fluctuations are built in following the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The effect of space discretization into cells in numerical hydrodynamics on the spatial correlation of fluctuations is studied with the help of static structure factor. A difference from the continuum result is pointed out and systematically investigated. Time evolution of the ensuing fluctuations is examined and the Green-Kubo formula is used for the extraction of shear viscosity from the fluctuations. The extracted value is demonstrated to be the same as the input value of the shear viscosity for the simulations using Israel-Stewart equations. It is also shown that numerical regulators commonly used in the codes to ensure stability of the calculation severely spoil the fluctuations and break the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.

title: A 4D $T^\prime$-expanded lattice QCD equation of state with a multi-dimensional 3D-Ising-type critical contribution
summary: Inferring the possible existence and location of a critical point on the QCD phase diagram through experimental observations requires equations of state that include both lattice QCD constraints and critical behavior. In this manuscript, we present the first four-dimensional equation of state in the $(T,μ_B,μ_Q,μ_S)$ space combining the lattice 4D $T^\prime$-Expansion Scheme with a critical contribution mapped from the 3D Ising model. We extend the earlier two-dimensional construction, the so-called Ising 2D-TExS in the $(T, μ_B)$ plane, promoting the critical point to a parametrizable critical surface in the full four-dimensional thermodynamic space. Our framework provides a family of equations of state to systematically study the effects of criticality in realistic hydrodynamic simulations with $BQS$ conserved charges, going beyond the case of strangeness neutrality, by varying the geometry of the critical surface and the strength of criticality at finite $μ_B$, $μ_Q$ and $μ_S$ separately.
